title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with a mix of geopolitical maneuvering and corporate machinations. From GPS jamming to SPAC deals, it seems everyone is trying to stake their claim in the final frontier.

themes.title: GPS Jamming Escalation
themes.body: Russia's renewed efforts to jam GPS signals over the Eastern Mediterranean are a stark reminder of the vulnerabilities in global navigation systems. This move not only complicates military operations but also raises questions about the resilience of commercial satellite networks.

themes.title: SPACs and Space Startups
themes.body: Quantum Space's decision to go public via a SPAC deal highlights the growing interest in space-related ventures, even as the IPO market remains shaky. Investors are clearly looking for the next big thing beyond Earth, but the sustainability of these ventures remains to be seen.

themes.title: U.S.-China Space Competition
themes.body: The upcoming WRC-27 conference is set to be a key battleground for U.S.-China tensions in space. As both nations vie for dominance in satellite communications and frequency allocations, the stakes are higher than ever.

themes.title: Defense Spending Trends
themes.body: The recent $1.4 billion boost to the space resilience line in the FY27 budget underscores a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. As threats evolve, so too does the funding landscape, with defense contractors poised to benefit.
